BL-991 — route-required-stages delivers a forward hop as addressed whenever the literal target is already a member of the effective set, so a coder addressing QA on a full-chain ticket jumps four declared stages and is merely recorded - the operator has ruled the declaration binding
What it solves: Source: the specifier's clarifying question to the operator, raised 2026-08-19 12:58 after QA flagged the coder sending two bounce-fixes straight to QA. Probing found no rule in `coder.prompt`, `QA.prompt` or `handoff-protocol.md` governing a bounce-fix's return path, so those jumps were un-governe…
Approval context: Two decisions are mine and worth your eye, since neither was settled by the ruling itself.
First, REWRITE rather than REFUSE. When a hop would jump a declared stage I have the router redirect it to the next declared stage, rather than refusing the send and making the agent re-address it. Rewriting …
BL-991 needs your approval before it can proceed. Reply here with "approve BL-991" (or "reject BL-991 <reason>") to act.
